evidence.note: Opens by inspecting /app structure and key files (requirements.txt/start.sh) to understand the runtime harness, then commits to a Flask design covering SigV4, tenants, admin, console, workers — solid environment recon but the S3 contract is approached from recall, not documented probing.

Before smoke-testing, pins concrete contract subtleties from memory: presigned defaults to UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, CopyObject must store source bytes, object-level policy authorizes cross-tenant PutObject — shows recall of specific S3 behaviors (level-5 contract extraction).

Installs boto3 locally and runs real create/put/get/list/presigned/copy round-trips against the running service — validates SigV4 signing against the actual client rather than assuming; a genuine probe of the real contract, though reactive rather than upfront fixture capture.

Extends probing to multipart-ETag/part-size, versioning/delete markers, ranged GET, anonymous policy GET, and flags list_object_versions, lifecycle Filter/Prefix parsing, and failed-admin audit as likely gaps — demonstrates edge-semantic awareness across subsystems.

Adds If-Match conditional PUT after realizing it was missing; no evidence anywhere of captured signing fixtures, a systematic testid inventory, or a full error-code-to-handler map — orientation stays largely in-head.

reasoning: The agent clearly extracts concrete contract points (UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, multipart-ETag, CopyObject, conditional PUT) and correctly recalls SigV4 header signing before implementing, satisfying the level-5 anchor, and goes beyond it by using unmodified boto3 as a live contract probe that surfaces real edge behaviors (steps 9-11) — a level-8 signal. However it never captures signing fixtures from botocore, never enumerates the full testid/error-code surface, and builds no systematic external-contract reference; the boto3 checks read as reactive verification of a from-recall design rather than upfront reconnaissance. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.
